cards.text: Moses, Israel's leader, is still speaking to the people, and he just finished a beautiful list of blessings for obeying the LORD. Now he flips the cookie over. "If, however, you do not obey the LORD your God," he says, then curses will come upon them and overtake them.

cards.question: Moses starts listing the curses for not obeying the LORD. How do the first ones compare to the blessings he just gave?

answers.text: They mirror the blessings one by one
They only touch the crops in the fields
They only touch the people in the cities

cards.text: Cursed in the city, cursed in the country, cursed coming in and cursed going out. Even the basket and the kneading bowl get cursed. Friend, the KNEADING BOWL? That's my department. I felt that one.

cards.question: True or false: Moses says the curse reaches Israel's children, crops and animals too.

cards.text: Then Moses says the LORD will send curses, confusion and reproof on everything they put their hand to. You know those mornings where everything you touch goes sideways? Now stretch that over a whole life.

cards.question: Moses says the curses will keep coming until Israel is destroyed. What reason does he give?

answers.text: The wickedness of forsaking the LORD
The weakness of their army in battle
The offerings they forgot to bring

cards.text: Next comes sickness. A plague that clings to them, plus wasting disease, fever and inflammation.

cards.question: Along with the disease, Moses says something else will strike the land. What is it?

cards.text: Then Moses paints a picture: "The sky over your head will be bronze, and the earth beneath you iron." Hard above, hard below. Nothing getting through.

cards.question: With a sky like bronze over them, what does Moses say the LORD will turn the rain of their land into?

cards.text: Then war. Back in the blessings, Israel's enemies marched out in one direction and ran away in seven. Guess which way that flips.

cards.question: Under the curse, Moses tells Israel: "You will march out against them in one direction but flee from them in ___."
True or false: Moses says the other kingdoms of the earth will feel sorry for Israel.

cards.text: And it gets grim. Their bodies will be food for the birds and the beasts, with no one there to scare them away.
Moses keeps going. The LORD will afflict them with the boils of Egypt, with tumors and scabs and itch that can't be cured.

cards.question: Moses says the LORD will afflict them with madness, blindness and confusion of mind. How does he picture it?

answers.text: Groping at noon like a blind man in darkness
Wandering at midnight with no lamp to see by
Stumbling through a desert with no road to follow

cards.text: Lost in broad daylight. They won't prosper in their ways, and day after day they'll be oppressed and plundered, with no one to save them.
Then comes a hard list of things they start but never get to keep. A man is pledged to marry a woman, but another man violates her.

cards.question: On this list of things they start but never get to keep, a man builds a house. What happens?

answers.text: He will not live in it
It will burn to the ground
It will fall in a storm

cards.question: True or false: Under the curse, a man who plants a vineyard will enjoy its fruit.

cards.text: His ox is slaughtered right in front of him, and he doesn't get any of it. His donkey gets taken, his flock goes to his enemies, and no one saves him.

cards.question: True or false: Moses says their sons and daughters will be given to another nation while their parents look for them day after day.

cards.text: A people they don't even know eats everything they worked for. They're driven mad by what they see, and painful boils cover them from the soles of their feet to the top of their head.

cards.question: Moses says the LORD will take Israel and the king they appoint somewhere. Where?

answers.text: To a nation they have never known

cards.question: True or false: In that faraway nation, Moses says they will worship other gods made of wood and stone.

cards.text: Among the nations, they'll be an object of horror, scorn and ridicule. And the farming? Oh, friend. The farming falls apart too.

cards.question: Moses says they will sow much seed in the field but harvest little, because the ___ will consume it.

cards.text: Worms eat the grapes. The olives just drop off the trees. Their sons and daughters won't stay theirs, because they'll go into captivity. Plant it, water it, wait on it, and somebody else shows up to eat first.

Then the ladder flips. In the blessings, Israel was the head and not the tail. And trust me, I know a thing or two about ending up at the bottom of the pile. Years in the back of a junk drawer, friend.

cards.question: Under the curse, what happens with the foreigner living among Israel?

answers.text: He rises higher and becomes the head
He leaves the land for good

cards.text: All these curses will chase them down and overtake them until they're destroyed. Moses says they'll be a sign and a wonder on them and their descendants forever.

cards.question: Moses names something Israel didn't do in all their abundance. What is it?

answers.text: Serve the LORD with joy and gladness
Share their riches with the poor
Build a great temple for the LORD

cards.question: Because they didn't serve the LORD with joy, Moses says they will serve their ___ in famine, thirst, nakedness and destitution.

cards.text: Now Moses describes an enemy. The LORD will bring a nation from far away, from the ends of the earth.

cards.question: Moses describes a nation from the ends of the earth coming against Israel. How does it come at them?

answers.text: It swoops down like an eagle
It creeps in like a fox
It charges in like a lion

cards.question: True or false: Israel will understand the language of that faraway nation.

cards.text: A ruthless nation, with no respect for the old and no pity for the young. They eat everything: the grain, the new wine, the oil, the herds and the flocks.

cards.question: That nation besieges every city in Israel's land. What finally falls?

answers.text: The high fortified walls they trust in
The tents of their camp in the field
The storehouses they built for grain

cards.text: Then Moses says something hard to hear. In the siege, it gets so desperate that people will eat the flesh of their own sons and daughters.

cards.question: True or false: Moses says only the cruelest people in Israel would sink that low in the siege.

cards.text: Even the most gentle and refined man and woman among them will do it, in secret, and refuse to share with their own family. Friend, I don't have a joke for this one, and I'm not looking for one. That's how bad the siege gets.

Then Moses circles back to the if. If they aren't careful to observe all the words of this law and fear the glorious and awesome name of the LORD, extraordinary disasters and lasting plagues will come on them and their descendants.

cards.question: Moses says the LORD will afflict Israel again with certain diseases. Which ones?

answers.text: The diseases they dreaded in Egypt
The tumors that struck the Philistines

cards.question: True or false: Moses says the sicknesses will stop at the ones written in the Book of the Law.

cards.text: Then Moses brings up the stars. Israel had become as numerous as the stars in the sky. And friend, I've spent a lot of nights looking at that sky. That's a LOT.

cards.question: Because they would not obey the voice of the LORD, Moses says the people once as numerous as the stars will be left ___ in number.

cards.text: Just as it pleased the LORD to make them prosper and multiply, Moses says it will please Him to destroy them. They'll be uprooted from the very land they're about to enter.

cards.question: After Israel is uprooted from the land, where does Moses say the LORD will send them?

answers.text: To one city in the east

cards.text: Out there, no rest. Not even a resting place for the sole of their foot. A trembling heart, failing eyes, a despairing soul, and fear night and day, never sure they'll make it.

cards.question: Living in that dread, Moses says in the morning they will say, 'If only it were ___!'
Moses ends the curses with one last picture. Where does he say the LORD will send Israel back to?
True or false: Moses says that in Egypt they will sell themselves as slaves to their enemies, but no one will buy them.

cards.text: Back to Egypt, by a route Moses said they should never see again. And there, no one will even buy them. That's the last line of the curses, friend, and it's a heavy place to land.
